title: 💻 Setting default compiler on Manjaro

messages.content: How to set default compiler to clang++ in Manjaro?

To set Clang as the default C++ compiler on Manjaro, follow these steps:

1. Open a terminal.
2. Check if Clang is installed by running the command:
```
clang++ --version
```
If Clang is not installed, you can do so by running the command:
```
sudo pacman -S clang
```
3. Set Clang as the default C++ compiler by creating (if it doesn't exist) or editing the file `/etc/profile.d/clang.sh`. You can use your favorite text editor, for example:
```
sudo nano /etc/profile.d/clang.sh
```
4. Add the following lines to the file:
```
export CXX=clang++
export CC=clang
```
5. Save and close the file.
6. To apply the changes, either log out and log back in, or source the file by running:
```
source /etc/profile.d/clang.sh
```
7. You can verify that Clang is now the default C++ compiler by running:
```
cpp --version
```
It should display the version information for Clang.

That's it! Clang should now be set as the default C++ compiler on your Manjaro system.
